content.v: 2026年全球游戏行业已记录10977个被裁岗位，接近1.1万人，超过2025年全年的9197人。ASGC游戏行业裁员追踪数据还显示，2024年仍是近三年裁员规模最大的一年，当年超过1.5万人失去相关岗位。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261103/1793656251_938211_jpg_r.jpg
距离2026年结束尚有两个月，行业裁员仍未停止。追踪方据此预计，全年被裁岗位可能升至约1.3万个，但该数字目前仅为预测，并非已经发生或获得企业确认的最终结果。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261103/1793656384_644196_jpg_r.jpg
EA、Ubisoft和Xbox被列为今年较突出的案例。Xbox旗下多家工作室此前数月已受到不同程度的裁员影响，未来还可能继续削减岗位。高昂的项目预算、持续增长的开发成本以及大型公司的重组，被认为是行业持续缩减人员的重要背景。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261103/1793656384_684464.jpg
参与成功作品的开发者同样难以获得长期岗位保障。PlayStation近期裁减了《羊蹄山之魂》开发人员，显示商业表现良好并不意味着团队能够避开后续调整。目前，各公司后续裁员规模以及全年约1.3万人的估算，仍有待进一步信息确认。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/thumbnews/20260720/1784518943_551412.jpg

items.title: 笼罩1.0评测
items.summary: The fog of war clears around Embervale, revealing a survival crafting masterpiece.

content.v: What is it? A high-fantasy survival crafting RPG set in the genre's most impressive sandbox. Release date: October 15, 2026 (1.0) Expect to pay: $40/£35 Developer: Keen Games Publisher: Keen Games Reviewed on: RTX 4080, AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D, 64GB RAM Steam Deck: Verified Link: Steam | Official site

High up on a mountain in the Albaneve Summits, just on the southern border of Enshrouded's new zone, I spot the perfect place for my next medieval building project. It seems safe with no nearby enemy spawns on the flat stretch of land, and there's even a cute frozen pond that gives it real Christmas-card appeal. I love it, and I'll love it even more once I've built a cliffside castle.

The only problem is I can't find a way up by climbing or gliding, so I'll have to make my own. I could build something, but that takes time, and I'm impatient. Instead, I behave like an absolute heathen—I bomb and pickaxe the hell out of the mountainside, carving a tunnel from the base to the top. It doesn't look great, but that's a problem for tomorrow's Flameborn.

That's always been one of my favorite parts of Enshrouded: you can destroy or build practically anything, anywhere in Embervale's voxel-based world. It's a survival crafting sandbox filled to the brim with handcrafted details, and every location still hidden by the fog of war could hold a new material, powerful weapon, or scenic vista. There's nothing quite like it, and just like the updates before, Enshrouded's 1.0 build keeps finding new, inventive ways to impress me long after I thought its well of surprises had run dry.
Built different

Enshrouded is a weird one. Not quite a traditional survival crafting game, but not a typical action RPG either. Its combat system and base building options are far more robust than most of its survival crafting cousins, but it's not nearly as brutal. I'm driven less by desperation and more by a desire to explore Embervale—a land devastated by a mysterious, malignant miasma known as ( you guessed it ) the Shroud. There's hardly a soul left in the world, so you learn more about its history from journals. Some are hastily scribbled by would-be heroes like you, while others are tragic retellings of someone's final days.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/eq6odqpoDXZb99JXjXgGeH.jpg
A few survivors remain as recruitable NPCs for your base. I love how lively they make player-made homes feel, even if the AI is a bit dopey.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/vcARrjYu4UMxMV8YnLsWkH.jpg

One of my favorite additions in 1.0 is the voiceover added to every journal. The same narrator reads them all, giving the whole thing an endearing storybook feel as he shifts tone and pitch for different authors.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/TbkyytePR5agJcPG9csrmH.jpg

I found my favorite journal in a tiny, mountainside cave left by an old man grieving his wife. You can wander around the surrounding area for more environmental storytelling, but I have to warn you: some details got me teary-eyed.

So, for what must be the millionth time in my career, I stumble out of a mystical, sleepy haze confused and poorly dressed for the world I've awakened to. I am the Flameborn—a sort of ordained-by-god chosen one and the last hope for restoring the ruins of Embervale—but for now, I certainly don't feel that way. I just feel like some guy. It's a title I'll have to grow into, but will have to wait until I've upgraded from the aptly named 'ragged armor set'. Yeesh.

Enshrouded follows most of those rags-to-riches genre basics, so of course I'll graduate from an era of fighting with sticks and eating fistfuls of berries to magic-infused swords and Michelin-star meals. I've played so many of these games that the flow comes naturally now, but what I like most about Enshrouded's take on classic survival systems is that it drops the more punitive elements like fatigue, crafting chance, and even structural integrity.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/FCNih4adSUA94YgAkXcHj9.jpg
Enshrouded has a robust set of custom difficulty options, but I learned the hard way to leave them alone until after you've tried the first dungeon.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/h7BYDohkAimUFP3zpaK4uN.jpg
An early access update added a custom setting for dehydration and starvation, but I much prefer playing without it .
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/Xgokkmf6vto3BFNdYNpFfA.jpg
There's cooking, farming, and even animal husbandry. Those systems are compelling enough as is, and don't gain anything by adding do-this-or-die mechanics.

Enshrouded knows that I, much like the family Golden Retriever, am treat-motivated. As long as there's shelter, fire, and decor, I'll get a stamina-boosting buff just by hanging out at home, but I'll never die from lack of sleep. In that regard, it's more like Valheim. Unique furnishings have their own comfort stats too, so there's incentive to explore Embervale for a new rug, fireplace, or even a toilet if you want a longer, more powerful boost. It's an especially exciting system for players like me, someone who loves building and decorating bases, but rarely sees a reward for the extra effort.

All this meticulous decorating makes me wonder whether I really want Enshrouded to add enemy raids on player bases and risk destroying them, but I'm leaning toward yes. It's the one major survival mechanic I miss in its formula, and I can't help but wistfully remember how fun it is to scramble into action when Valheim warns, "The forest is moving..." Imagine that, but with Enshrouded's poisonous fog instead.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/FLxfLR3adowQi78jtaFcWH.jpg

Enshrouded has always been my favorite survival-crafting block set, but I'm thrilled with the new build camera. Building in tight corners is less hassle, and I don't slide off the roof a dozen times..
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/gc8RmHTqDwvon5nmMP9VeH.jpg

There's got to be a high fantasy Ikea hidden somewhere in Embervale, because the amount of furniture and decor in Enshrouded is absurd. It's nice to go from picking at scraps to being overwhelmed by choice
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/jXrGxqZa57h2Wi2xRQPyhH.jpg

Version 1.0 also added Sparkworks, a logic system for creating your own enemy spawns, player-triggered events, special world builds, custom dungeons, and more. Your creations are shareable, too, so other players can suffer through your cruel obstacle course designs. I've tinkered with it myself, but I've mostly spent my time exploring player-made hobbit holes and feeling painfully self-conscious by comparison.
Fog of war

Repetitive tasks—another hunt for a rare material, another trek across the map—can become exasperating even in the best survival crafting games. There's a thin line between tedium and satisfaction, and Enshrouded walks it better than most. Much of that is thanks to the game's philosophy around punishment and reward, but its RPG elements add a layer of complexity that more than makes up for anything missing from Enshrouded's "survival-lite" approach.

Take my group, for example. I play with seven other friends, while that feels like a lot for most survival crafting games, Enshrouded's combat roles give us distinctly useful jobs. Rather than dumping points into three or four barebones stats, your Flameborn can specialize across 12 different skill trees. I mostly opt for tank, athlete, and assassin perks, but my allies fill other needs with mix-and-match builds for glass-cannon wizards, battlemage healers, or stealthy assassins. We also have our preferred responsibilities, like mining, woodcutting, gardening, cooking, and all those other usual genre chores.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/LPAC3DDjRy5kCy55FcJGqN.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/2EC48nXTu9pahry4PtntqN.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/FVwEWtH3LJvQVB5AzNzytN.jpg

content.v: 《大神》续作公布近两年后，距离正式亮相仍有一段时间。Clovers创始人兼导演神谷英树坦言，公众期待持续升高，也让他承受了更大压力，因此建议玩家“不要抱太多期待”。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261103/1793655597_570003_jpg_r.jpg
神谷英树在2026年卢卡漫画与游戏节接受采访时表示，这部续作已经成为自己的一项使命。过去开发全新游戏时，外界没有既定预期，作品也更具未知性；此次着手续作后，他明显感受到玩家期待不断增长。
Clovers正在吸纳曾参与初代《大神》《猎天使魔女》等作品的资深开发者。续作将采用RE引擎制作，计划延续前作的美术风格和故事，主角天照也将回归。Capcom对Clovers保持信任，并在开发过程中采取较少干预的方式。
初代《大神》于2006年推出，虽然获得高度评价，但未取得商业成功。不过该作一直受到一批忠实玩家喜爱。目前续作正式名称尚未确定，发售日期、实机内容及登陆平台也均未公布。

others.title: 《影之刃零》借鉴塞尔达？制作人澄清：纯中国文化

content.v: 近日《 影之刃零 》开发总监梁其伟确认，游戏中梅谷湖直接以中国武侠文化为灵感，并非向《塞尔达传说：风之杖》致敬。玩家可以乘船往来于不同岛屿，在未知中逐一探索。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261103/1793657260_486656_jpg_r.jpg
梅谷湖的航行体验曾令人联想到《塞尔达传说：风之杖》中横渡海拉鲁大海、穿梭于岛屿之间的过程。面对两者是否存在灵感关系的问题，梁其伟表示，许多游戏都塑造过令人难忘的湖泊环境，但梅谷湖采用的是武侠文化中的湖泊意象。
梁其伟解释称，湖泊是武侠作品中具有代表性的环境，“江湖”也常与“武林”并用，用来指代整个武侠世界。在他的构想中，岛屿既可与大陆相连，也能完全隔绝，岛上还可设置隐藏宝藏、奇异敌人以及笼罩在谜团中的传说，为玩家提供持续发现的机会。
实际体验中，梅谷湖各座岛屿呈现出不同氛围，宝藏和敌人的配置也不相同，其中不止一座岛屿与主线故事密切相关。这些设计让视觉与游玩体验上的相似联想，和场景真正采用的文化来源有了明确区别。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/thumbnews/20260720/1784518943_551412.jpg

content.v: 《GTA6》与《塞尔达：时之笛 重制版》计划于2026年11月相隔数周上市。外媒TheVerge认为，两款作品的同月交锋虽然引人关注，却更像游戏行业旧时代的回声，其热度无法掩盖行业面临的普遍困境。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261103/1793654269_538799_jpg_r.jpg
《GTA6》是R星历经13年打造的新作。Circana估算，29%的美国玩家有意购买该作，其需求甚至可能推动PS5和Xbox Series主机销售。《给他爱5》自2013年发售以来销量已达2.3亿份，并连续13年进入美国年度畅销游戏前20名。
任天堂则将《塞尔达：时之笛 重制版》作为假日档重要独占游戏。该作既承担经典作品现代化的任务，又将在《塞尔达传说》真人电影2027年上映前推出，这让任天堂有底气与R星正面竞争。
不过2026年的游戏行业仍面临大规模裁员、工作室关闭、硬件成本上升、服务型游戏承压及AI工具带来的不确定性。任天堂掌握软硬件生态，R星则受益于前作的长期成功，这两种条件均难以复制，因此两款超级作品的热度不能被视为解决行业困境的通用办法。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/thumbnews/20260720/1784518943_551412.jpg

content.v: 近日前Xbox首席运营官蒋海伦公开回应离职争议，明确否认自己因违反政策被解雇，但没有说明离职的直接原因。她表示，外界流传的相关说法并不准确，此事也“不是完整故事”。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261103/1793653989_601212_jpg_r.jpg
蒋海伦曾在微软任职超过20年，于2026年7月升任Xbox首位首席运营官，负责内容、硬件、平台和服务等业务的整体损益，约三个月后离职。此前有匿名消息称她因违反政策被解雇，另有信源和记者支持这一说法，但所谓违规的具体性质始终没有明确。
蒋海伦在题为“Clarity is Kindness”的LinkedIn文章中逐项否认向记者泄露机密、离职后加入竞争对手、歧视、霸凌、骚扰、内幕交易、挪用公款及其他欺诈行为，也否认自己因未获更高职位而离开。她称自己只参加过公司授权的采访，发文前也未接触曾向她询问此事的记者。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261103/1793653761_302436_jpg_r.jpg
她同时表示，自己对公平和问责标准在此事中的执行方式存在严重关切。微软发言人称公司不讨论个别人事事项；前Xbox高管Shannon Loftis公开声援蒋海伦，Xbox负责人Asha Sharma则表示未来会更新首席运营官职位安排。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/thumbnews/20260720/1784518943_551412.jpg

content.v: 近日前Xbox首席运营官Helen Chiang公开回应突然离开微软一事，否认自己因违反公司政策被解雇。她表示相关描述并不准确，其此前保持沉默也不代表认同外界说法。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261103/1793653761_302436_jpg_r.jpg
Chiang在LinkedIn发布了题为“Clarity is Kindness”的离职说明。她已在微软工作27年，其中相当一部分经历与《我的世界》业务有关，并于数周前突然离开Xbox。
针对围绕离职原因的猜测，Chiang逐项否认曾向媒体泄露公司机密、准备加入微软竞争对手，以及涉及歧视、霸凌、骚扰、内幕交易、挪用公款或其他欺诈行为。她也否认离职与未能获得更高职位有关，称自己自2011年以来没有参加过职位面试，最近的职务是公司在7月晋升后作出的安排，并非由她主动索求。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261103/1793653989_601212_jpg_r.jpg
Chiang表示她原本希望继续留在微软参与建设，不接受有关其能力、野心或严重丑闻的说法。她同时对公司在其个案中运用公平与问责标准的方式提出严重质疑，但没有公开离职过程的完整细节。目前能够确认的是Chiang已否认相关指控，双方尚未就事实达成一致。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/thumbnews/20260720/1784518943_551412.jpg

content.v: Alinea Analytics估算，Screen Burn开发的第一人称 恐怖 游戏《寂静岭：小镇陷落》自首发以来售出约40.4万份，按50美元售价计算，收入约为2020万美元。这些数字并非科乐美公布的正式业绩。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261103/1793653718_122016_jpg_r.jpg
从估算数据来看，PS5版占游戏总销量的70.9%，实体版则贡献了42.8%的收入。实体收入所占比例也被用于讨论实体发行的重要性，以及PlayStation计划自2028年1月起放弃实体媒介的决定。
这一成绩低于系列近年的另外两部作品。《寂静岭2：重制版》前三天销量超过100万份，《寂静岭f》首日便达到同一里程碑。不过后两作获得的评价明显更好，登陆平台也更多，不能只凭销量数字直接判断《寂静岭：小镇陷落》市场表现。
《寂静岭：小镇陷落》发售时还面临较为密集的竞争，前后有《控制：共振》《鬼武者：剑之道》《黎明行者之血》等作品争夺关注。

content.v: 动视已就《使命召唤：现代 战争 4》使用梨泰院踩踏事故影像致歉，并承诺在11月12日发布的下一次游戏更新中彻底移除相关素材。遇难者家属及韩国玩家团体此前公开提出删除要求。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261103/1793653283_189551_jpg_r.jpg
争议画面出现在游戏开场片头中。该片头通过新闻报道蒙太奇呈现虚构的朝鲜全面入侵韩国情节，其间穿插真实历史影像。一段医护人员为倒地者实施心肺复苏的短暂画面，随后被玩家认出来自2022年首尔梨泰院万圣节人群踩踏事故后的新闻报道。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261103/1793653284_758157_jpg_r.jpg
梨泰院事故发生在人群密集的街头活动期间，狭窄巷道内出现人群挤压，造成159人死亡、196人受伤。相关影像被用于虚构战争背景后，10·29梨泰院惨案遇难者家属协会与韩国游戏用户协会公开抗议，并要求动视删除素材。
动视表示，《使命召唤：现代战争4》是为营造真实沉浸感而创作的虚构作品，使用真实新闻广播画面无意唤起或淡化包括梨泰院踩踏事故在内的任何悲剧。公司同时向因此受到伤害的遇难者家属、受害者及其他受影响者致歉，相关画面定于11月12日通过游戏更新移除。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/thumbnews/20260720/1784518943_551412.jpg

content.v: 《最终幻想：共鸣》制作人Keisuke Nakashima回顾称，他在2020年提出将手游《最终幻想：勇气启示录》的内容扩展为正式主机作品时，曾遭到史克威尔艾尼克斯部分管理层抵触。面对成本更低、制作更快的基础移植方案，他坚持面向主机重新打造完整的游戏体验。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261103/1793652657_284510_jpg_r.jpg
Nakashima表示，他曾在手游宣传行程中听到玩家反馈：有人对作品感兴趣，却因抽卡要素放弃游玩。这段经历促使团队尝试通过主机版本接触更广泛的受众。
《最终幻想：共鸣》的改编方式与《歧路旅人0》相似，后者取材自《歧路旅人：大陆的霸者》。两款作品都吸收了原手游的部分故事，并在主机版本中移除微交易和抽卡系统。
《最终幻想：勇气启示录》现已停止运营，因此《最终幻想：共鸣》也承担了保存其部分内容与玩家记忆的作用。不过，新作采用HD-2D画面和回合制玩法，并非把原手游直接搬到新平台。
《最终幻想：共鸣》后来创下《最终幻想》系列单机作品在Steam上最高同时在线峰值。有分析师估算本作发售不足五天便在PS5、XSX和Steam售出约40万份，收入约2000万美元。

content.v: 宝可梦公司日本官方社交账号近期连续发布带有宝可梦角色和数字的图片，数字还在逐次下降。部分玩家据此推测，这组内容可能在11月30日归零，届时或有某种公告。

content.v: 近日任天堂公开《塞尔达：时之笛 重制版》开发者访谈，确认本作将保留彼此分隔的区域地图，不会把海拉鲁改造成无缝开放世界。团队希望借助场景切换延续原作的探索节奏与期待感。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261103/1793653399_792926_jpg_r.jpg
游戏导演HokWai Ng表示，各地点的独特氛围及其连接方式是原作体验的重要部分。重制版因此没有照搬《塞尔达传说：旷野之息》和《塞尔达传说：王国之泪》的连续大地图结构。玩家切换区域时既能回顾此前经历，也会对下一处场景产生期待。Ng将项目原则概括为“视觉可以变化、体验不能改变”。
这一原则也影响了海拉鲁平原的美术设计。美术总监Aya Shida介绍，可探索区域拥有较高的细节密度，无法抵达的地方则会减少视觉信息，呈现为远方景色；城堡、风车等地标也被适当放大，以形成尺度变化。环境画面还会帮助玩家判断可破坏物体后方是否可能藏有内容，或某处能否充当观察点。
美术团队早期以“木偶戏般的感觉”和“实拍特效电影的模拟质感”描述目标风格，希望世界具有真实感，但不采用严格写实的表现方式。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/thumbnews/20260720/1784518943_551412.jpg

content.v: 《守望先锋》团队正在筹备一次面向2027年2月的大型发布，内容包括新内容、多项功能以及玩家经常接触的系统改进。在2026年推出十名新英雄并推进“利爪统治”故事线后，团队已将工作重点延伸至下一年。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261103/1793652151_185579_jpg_r.jpg
游戏总监Aaron Keller表示，团队希望每年年初都能推出具有足够影响力的变化，但不想让玩家觉得开发组只是在按照固定模板重复发布内容。他认为，稳定带来大型内容能够增强玩家对游戏长期发展的信心，也表明团队和公司将继续投入多年。
随着英雄阵容继续扩大，副游戏总监Alex Dawson承认，让新角色和新机制始终保持《守望先锋》的整体感正变得更加困难。团队已经调整内部试玩方式，并会反复判断新增内容是否符合游戏的核心体验。开发组认为仍有不少角色构想和原型可以探索，同时也讨论过未来改变内容扩充方式的可能性。
针对英雄皮肤分配不均的问题，Keller表示，团队知道部分英雄长期缺少高规格外观。虽然制作能力持续提高，资源配置仍需兼顾商业支持：每赛季推出的多款神话皮肤中，通常会有一款分配给较能推动营收的英雄，另一款则倾向于近期较少获得神话皮肤或其他皮肤的英雄。

items.title: Xbox 首席运营官在仅仅 3 个月后离开，驳斥了她“因违反政策而被解雇”的说法，称她的故事是关于“核心价值观”的
items.summary: Helen Chiang, who became the Xbox division's first chief operating officer in July, says she has "serious conc

content.v: Longtime Microsoft executive Helen Chiang was made Xbox's first-ever chief operating officer as part of the 'reset' in July, a role that gave her "end-to-end P&L responsibility across content, hardware, platform, and services." Then, just three months later and with virtually no fanfare, she was gone , amidst an anonymous claim that she was "terminated for policy violations."
Saying it was important "to set the record straight," Chiang has now formally denied that claim in a lengthy LinkedIn post, saying she did not:

The record-straightening did not get into why Chiang did leave Xbox, although she seemed to imply that it was not an amicable departure: "I believe in fairness, accountability, and holding ourselves to the standards we expect of others. Those standards only mean something when they're applied consistently. I have serious concerns about how they were applied in my case, and I believe those concerns deserve to be taken seriously."

The sudden split seemed doubly strange because prior to taking the COO job at Xbox, Chiang spent more than 20 years at Microsoft, nearly all of it with the Xbox division—rising from Xbox platform business manager in 2007 to corporate vice president of the Minecraft franchise in 2020, a position she held for more than six years. The memo announcing Chiang's departure was also notably restrained: "Helen Chiang is leaving Microsoft today," Xbox CEO Asha Sharma wrote. "I'm grateful for her years of service and wish her well."

"I share this because I don't want my departure reduced to an inaccurate story about incompetence, ambition for the next big job, or a Nelson-level scandal. My story is about staying true to your core values, especially when it is hard. That's the legacy I hope to leave behind," Chiang wrote in her message.
"This is not how I ever imagined my story here would end. And it is not the whole story."
I've reached out to Microsoft for comment on Chiang's message and will update if I receive a reply.

items.title: 前 Xbox 高管分享她神秘离职后的故事
items.summary: Helen Chiang, the veteran Xbox staffer who got promoted in July and left the company amid mysterious circumsta

content.v: Helen Chiang, the veteran Xbox staffer who got promoted in July and left the company amid mysterious circumstances just recently , has shared her side of the story--but her response doesn't close the book on this saga.

In a LinkedIn post titled "Clarity is Kindess," which itself is a reference to her former boss (and Xbox CEO) Asha Sharma's much-ridiculed and cringey mantra, said it's "not accurate" that she was "fired for a policy violation" as multiple reports said.

Chiang said she will not "turn this into a play-by-play" and reveal the specifics, but she wanted to speak out to dispel rumors. "What has been said about my departure, and what has been left unsaid, has created a picture of me that I hardly recognize."
https://www.gamespot.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Xbox.png?w=636

She went on to "set the record straight" by claiming she did not leak confidential company information to the press as some had speculated. "I have never communicated with any journalist outside the limited, company-authorized interviews I’ve done as part of my job," she said, adding that this includes having no contact with any journalist who reached out to her before today to ask for her side of the story.

Chiang went on to say she did not leave Xbox to join a competitor. "You don’t spend two decades somewhere without developing a deep loyalty to the people, teams, and businesses you’ve helped build," she said
"Xbox was never just another stop in my career. My end game was always to keep building here," she said.
That may all be true, but it's also unquestionable that people regularly spend lengthy periods of their career at one company, in high-level positions, and then move to other companies.
Third, Chiang said she "did not engage in discrimination, bullying, harassment, insider trading, embezzlement, or other fraudulent activity."
"I stand by my record: both the results I delivered and the way I have treated people throughout my career. I won’t let speculation define my character or erase that record," she said.

Chiang added that she did not leave Xbox because she was "passed over for a bigger role." She said that since having children, she became more "intentional about how I define ambition and success." She said she has purposefully not sought out bigger roles or jobs with more responsibilities; she said she hadn't interviewed for a job since 2011.

"My reputation and results paved the way for the opportunities that followed. I went where the company believed I was needed and where I could have the greatest impact," she said, adding that she did not ask to become Xbox's first-ever COO.
"I believe in fairness, accountability, and holding ourselves to the standards we expect of others. Those standards only mean something when they’re applied consistently," she said.
Chiang said she has "serious concerns" about how those standards were applied in her case, and she said those concerns "deserve to be taken seriously."

"I share this because I don’t want my departure reduced to an inaccurate story about incompetence, ambition for the next big job, or a Nelson-level scandal. My story is about staying true to your core values, especially when it is hard," she said. "That’s the legacy I hope to leave behind."

Chiang's statement doesn't spell out the specific nature surrounding her departure from Xbox, so many will naturally want more answers. Those could come in time, as Chiang said this is "not the whole story."

Another former Xbox executive, Shannon Loftis, commented on Chiang's post to say she is "Team Helen all the way." Loftis said she wonders who may have leaked the "false information" about Chiang and what their motivations may have been. In any event, she says it shows a "loss of moral character and 'clarity' in leadership at Xbox."

"A real leadership team would have relentlessly pursued the 'leaker' and taken appropriate action because 'confidential personnel matters' actually are bases for defamation lawsuits," she said. "It's a clownshow up in there and I feel terrible for anyone that still has to deal with it."
A spokesperson for Microsoft told Windows Central that the company does not “discuss individual personnel matters.”

According to a source speaking to Eurogamer , Chiang was “terminated for policy violations.” The Verge’s Tom Warren backed this up , saying Chiang was cut loose due to a “policy violation,” but the exact nature of that is unknown.
In July, Sharma announced that Chiang would become Xbox’s first-ever COO, with “end-to-end” responsibility for the financial future of Xbox’s content, hardware, platform, and services.

Chiang had worked at Microsoft for 20 years, in that time playing a key role in the creation of Xbox Live and later shepherding Mojang and the lucrative Minecraft franchise. As COO, Chiang was expected to “bring our businesses together under one operating model, making sure we make clear investment decisions, learn from our successes and failures, and hold ourselves accountable for results,” Sharma said.
For her part, Sharma said she will have an update to share on the COO position at Xbox at some point, but she didn’t divulge more.

The Xbox business was “not healthy” when Sharma took over, she said, and Chiang no doubt had a challenging road ahead of her. As for now, however, people can only speculate as to the real reason she left Xbox.

items.title: 创意总监表示《异形：隔离2》坚持纯粹的生存恐怖根源
items.summary: Alien Isolation 2 will be released in 2027, ready to remind you why xenomorphs are pure nightmare fuel. At the

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/06/05/alienisolation-thumb-1780701533804.jpg

Alien: Isolation 2 will be released in 2027, ready to remind you why xenomorphs are pure nightmare fuel. At the Lucca Comics and Games Festival IGN sat down with the game's creative director, Al Hope, who explained the core vision behind the science fiction sequel and why the team was sticking with the survival horror genre.

"We feel like there's still so much to mine or tap into in the universe of that first movie," he said. "We feel like in Alien: Isolation 2, I think the promise is about transporting you back to that time and place, that window of the timeline where just one alien can be absolutely terrifying and an incredible challenge, an incredible experience."

The original Alien: Isolation , released in 2014, had engineer Amanda (daughter of Ellen) Ripley as its star, as she searched for clues relating to her mother's disappearance on the space station Sevastopol. We've already heard Andrea Deck, Ripley’s voice actor, during a press demo for the sequel, but Hope was keen to underline the fact that Alien Isolation 2 is very focused on its new protagonist.

"We're really proud of Amanda, but to be clear, you're playing as a new character in Isolation 2... She works for the company; she hasn't encountered the creature before. And so yeah, I guess we're super excited about Blake."

We know a little about Blake already. She's a manager at Weyland-Yutani and has just arrived on planet LV-921 in search of the lab that was jettisoned from Sevastopol Station by Amanda Ripley, complete with a xenomorph hanging around inside.

You can read the full interview with Creative Director Al Hope and Project Art Director Ana Sopikova here , where we also talk xenomorph design, seeing the first game's save stations appear in Alien: Romulus , and whether or not the games are now part of the official Alien canon.

items.title: 《使命召唤：战区》本周将添加天气系统
items.summary: Call of Duty: Warzone is adding a weather system that will make every match feel a bit different.

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/10/30/callofduty-mw4-dmz-review-blogroll-1793400702051.jpg
Call of Duty: Warzone is adding a weather system that will make every match feel a bit different.

Later this week, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's Season 1 update will be released, and with it will come big changes to Warzone. Developer Raven Software is adding a bunch of content that matches the mechanics and tone Modern Warfare 4 brought to the franchise last month. One of the biggest things that's coming to Warzone is a new weather system, which means the map might have rain, wind, or other effects when you drop in.

It sounds like the weather will be determined before you ever load into the match, so don't expect weather cycles as you'd see in a game like Grand Theft Auto. The goal is to make it so Warzone matches feel different every time you play, as the battle royale's maps have been pretty stagnant for the last six years. The weather never changes, which can eventually make the maps feel a bit boring. However, this may make the game feel consistently interesting, and something like rain may have slight changes to gameplay. It could impact visibility, make your footsteps louder as they splash in puddles, and more.

Earlier this fall, Wardogs also added weather to multiplayer matches , which had some big changes for the gameplay. It's a worthy change to Call of Duty's battle royale and one that fans have wanted to see for some time. Fans have also wanted to see a day/night cycle as well, which could make something like night-vision goggles a meaningful piece of gear. NVGs are part of the game's DMZ extraction mode, though they're primarily used for enclosed facilities that have no power.
The new Call of Duty: Warzone update will launch with two new maps on November 6 as part of Modern Warfare 4 Season 1.

items.title: 《异形：隔离 2》开发者透露新主角、星球设定和 1979 年电影根源
items.summary: IGN sat down with Creative Director Al Hope and Project Art Director Ana Sopikova to discuss why Alien: Isolat

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/06/10/alien-isolation-blog-1781092645754.jpg

It's been 12 years since Alien: Isolation first introduced us to the unique terror of being trapped with a Xenomorph, and now Creative Assembly is finally ready to drag us kicking and screaming back into its nightmare. With Alien: Isolation 2 set for release next year, the studio is returning to the survival horror roots that made the original such a cult classic, but this time with a new protagonist, a new location, and plenty of fresh opportunities to be horribly murdered by everyone's favorite acid-blooded nightmare.

At the Lucca Comics and Games Festival, IGN sat down with Creative Director Al Hope and Project Art Director Ana Sopikova to discuss why the sequel took so long, how Ridley Scott's original 1979 movie continues to shape the game's design, and what fans can expect from this long-awaited return. We also talked Alien canon, Amanda Ripley's role, and whether there's already an Alien: Isolation 3 lurking somewhere in Hope's imagination.

IGN: The first Alien movie was a horror movie, and then they moved on to action and other genres. Both of the Alien Isolation games are survival horror games. Was there ever any idea of making Alien Isolation 2 in a different genre?

Al Hope: No, it's a short answer to that. I guess we absolutely adore that first movie and, obviously, Isolation, but we feel like there's still so much to mine or tap into in the universe of that first movie. And it felt like we wanted to tell other stories in the same part of that space of the universe in the same kind of context. So yeah, no, I guess we feel like in Alien Isolation 2, I think the promise is about transporting you back to that time and place, that window of the timeline where just one alien can be absolutely terrifying and an incredible challenge, an incredible experience. And I suppose if you just wanted to explore that, go back and explore that and evolve it.
IGN: The Xenomorph is a very iconic monster character. Is it challenging designing a Xenomorph for this game that is part of this iconic kind of legacy?

Ana Sopikova: Well, of course. It's a great honor I think for all of us and especially for our team to just be able to contribute to such an iconic IP. I think to go back to what Al was saying, we are really staying true to Ridley Scott’s original 1979 film, and we have a really good close relationship with 20th Century [Studios]. We have an archive with just loads of behind-the-scenes photos from the set, just really close-up images that really allow the team to just go deep in there and study and look at the types of materials they used at the time and look at the types of methods that they were using for building this costume. And then we've just taken that and applied it to what we are doing for the game. And I think really in terms of designing, we are staying true to 1979.

So we're definitely not reinventing the wheel there. And fictionally, obviously in Isolation 2, as people might have seen from the trailer, they have recognized the Haz Lab. So it is the same creature that you encountered in the first game that landed on this new planet. So you can imagine it will be quite similar to what people have seen before, but we're still taking it a little bit further just again in terms of fidelity. Time has passed, there's new technology, and we can just afford a little bit more detail, a little bit of a shinier texture to put it safely. So yeah, there's still space for us to go deeper, but we're not deviating madly elsewhere because for us, really, 1979 is the focus.
https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/06/09/alien-isolation-2-preview-blogroll-1781007414832.jpg
IGN: Speaking of the movies, how did it feel to see the emergency phone save points from Alien: Isolation appear as a special Easter egg in Fede Álvarez's Alien: Romulus?

Al Hope: Just thinking about what you were saying there, I think the team feels really privileged to be in this space, and obviously we were absolutely blown away and thrilled when Fede Álvarez put the save station in Romulus.

I think that's the privilege. We get to work with this original source material and we have the potential to, we're helping grow it. And that is, I think, for all of us, such a privilege and so exciting, as well.

IGN: So just so I understand, because I know there was a lot spoken about that, what you just mentioned about what Fede Álvarez did. And so it's safe to assume that both of these games now kind of exist in the official canon of the Alien universe?

Al Hope: It's really ultimately for the fans [to decide]. I think they really embraced the first game, and I think that's what's important. Sure, there are timelines and all that stuff. That's cool. I think we're just really focused on trying to tell that next chapter.
IGN: Going in a different direction, obviously Amanda is in this game in some capacity. Can you speak to that at all?

Al Hope: Well, we're really proud of Amanda, but to be clear, you're playing as a new character in Isolation 2. And that felt like the natural choice for us. We wanted to tell a new story. It felt like the right way to do that would be in a new location, and being in a new location, then actually seeing it through the eyes of a new character, seemed to make a lot of sense for us. And a character that has a different perspective. She works for the company; she hasn't encountered the creature before. And so yeah, I guess we're super excited about Blake.

IGN: With the first game, one of the most popular mods was the VHS color filter. I don't want to spoil anything, but is there a chance that it makes some sort of official appearance in this game, or is that just a cool community thing that was the first game?

Ana Sopikova: Who knows? I mean, it was still quite early, so I'm not going to comment specifically. There will be a photo mode. I think we've just confirmed it in the Q&A recently. We spent actually a lot of time researching cameras and camera technology and looking at it through the lens of lo-fi sci-fi and just really being authentic to the tech and to the actual, I guess, the physical objects and physical technology. So we are viewing the photo mode through that lens. So who knows?
I think there's definitely going to be plenty of opportunities for fans to capture and express themselves.
IGN: Going back to the first game and the process, so it's been, what is it, 12 years since the first game. Why now? I guess just why now? Why is now the time to have a sequel to the original game?

Al Hope: Yeah, that's a good question. So I've been thinking about what we could do for a sequel before we'd actually released the first game. But I guess as a studio, we were busy, and I guess what we've benefited from is that decade of new players discovering the game and getting their feedback. And the short answer is it felt like the time was right to come back. And so yeah, just super thrilled to be having this opportunity with this really fantastic team, which is great because the team is this mix of people who worked on the first game, and then we've got really fantastic fresh new talent, new talent coming on board. So it's this really lovely combination.

items.title: 任天堂解释为何选择重制另一部《塞尔达传说：时之笛》
items.summary: Nintendo has explained why it chose to develop another The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake.

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/09/08/the-legend-of-zelda-40th-anniversary-direct-9-8-2026-00-54-51-1788877510793.png
Nintendo has explained why it chose to develop another The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake .

Franchise producer Eiji Aonuma was asked what sparked the team's desire to return to one of the most treasured stories in gaming history during the first installment in a series of Ask the Developer Q&A posts. It's an in-depth chat about what it was like to revisit a classic game for Nintendo Switch 2, and how it came about in the first place.

The reimagining set to launch in just a few short days will mark the second time Nintendo has remade The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (the first launched for the Nintendo 3DS in 2011 ). Aonuma explained that there were a number of factors Entertainment Planning & Development (EDP) Production Group No. 3 had in mind, with its 40th anniversary being one of the most important.

"This year marks the 40th anniversary of the very first Legend of Zelda game," Aonuma said. "With that in mind, I was thinking about what I should create as the producer of the series. Many of the team members who work alongside me on Legend of Zelda games today have only experienced developing the more recent titles. That led me to wonder, 'Do they truly understand just how significant The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time was to the series as a whole?'"

Aonuma makes a good point. Although he worked on the original Nintendo 64 game when it launched in 1998 and has carried that experience through subsequent entries in the series in the decades since, there are plenty of team members who don't have that same familiarity with its past.

Sure, there are those with a passing familiarity with the original The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time or those who have at least played it, but Aonuma started to wonder how they'd interpret the game "as they go about developing future Legend of Zelda games." Allowing them to not only revisit that original story but also leave their own stamp on it, he believes, could help bolster whatever new The Legend of Zelda games come next.

"By learning the game structure and development style behind the original The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, and by actually rebuilding it as a full remake," he added, "it may trigger new insights that they can carry forward into future development. If we could achieve that, I thought it would be incredibly valuable. That’s what led us to the conclusion that now is the right time to revisit The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time once again."

Aonuma elaborated, saying that there were many elements considered when choosing to develop a The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake for Switch 2. The team wanted players who had grown used to the open structure of games like Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom to enjoy the fun of "progressing through a carefully paced adventure and story" that is "gradually building up the player’s growth and their understanding of the narrative along the way."

Nintendo's latest The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake launches for Switch 2 November 5. Despite having decades of experience and solid reasoning backing the decision to do a remake, Aonuma recently said he's still "nervous" to see what players think . While we wait to get our hands on the launch build, you can see what IGN thought in our hands-on preview .

items.title: “有一些非常公平的批评”：《Arc Raiders》的开发人员理解为什么玩家对其人工智能的使用如此不满，但表示记录每一条语音“太不切实际”
items.summary: Embark has since re-recorded lines to inject more real human voices to the game.

content.v: The start of Arc Raiders was a very mixed bag. On one hand it managed to attract an unbelievable amount of players as Embark Studios struck gold with its gentler take on extraction shooters. But all of this hype was somewhat overshadowed by the controversy surrounding its use of AI to mimic voice actors and supplement the dialogue.

While the actors involved did sign contracts allowing Embark to do this, there was still a great deal of backlash from players who were frustrated to see AI injected into the game. Many players pointed out, rightfully so, just how lifeless, lacklustre, and odd some of the AI voicelines sounded, a fact that was made all the more apparent by how fantastic Marathon's NPCs were .
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/Fd4TUWBBCNNNPuCwFugtUZ-1920-80.jpg

Embark's devs have pointed out, however, that it only used AI in order to get updates out the door faster; that this was due to efficiency rather than an affinity for the technology. "[The actors] have been here all along," Embark's audio director Bence Pajor says. "But we haven't always used them to record the actual thing you're going [to hear] because that's only been solidified super late. We made a lot of training data from their voices so we could prototype as well with their voice.

"Every new item that appears in the game, every new feature, everything needs to have a lot of dialogue because you can ping it. There's so much going into everything. To record the training data for the ping system becomes too impractical to record every possible version of something. I mean the actors would just go crazy if they had to read all of that. That's not feasible because the game has been changing so fast and we can't call them in every time we just change a feature."

Since the controversy first erupted, Embark has stressed multiple times that it wants to support voice actors . "We are not in the industry of replacing actors, actually quite the opposite we should celebrate the performance and give them more space," chief creative officer Stefan Strandberg says. "And that is something that I'm hoping to bring to players over the coming years for Arc Raiders: really seeing what the characters are like and who they are, and what motivates them, making it real."

Arguably, though, the damage has already been done. Using AI to bulk up voice lines may be easier, and replacing it with real voice actors when you can is certainly better than the alternative, but it has still set a bad precedent for voice actors in an industry which is relentless in its attempt to cut creative corners to optimise costs.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/TCou4LpWxSUzfBu3QPeR6P-1920-80.jpg

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/11/02/godzilla-destroy-all-monsters-melee-remastered-blogroll-01-1793639559274.jpg

The first time I ever saw Japan's most famous kaiju on the big screen was in Godzilla 2000: Millennium. Like any nine-year-old kid, I was obsessed with Big G. I read the Dark Horse comics, and I taped all the movies I could on TV. Things were different then; Godzilla was a big deal, but theatrical releases for Godzilla films were incredibly rare in the States If you saw those movies, it was on TV and they were dubbed or edited versions released under different titles like Godzilla: King of the Monsters or Godzilla vs. The Sea Monster. After Godzilla 2000 underperformed, it took another five years for the series to see a theatrical release in the U.S. – and into that void stomped 2002’s Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee.

It was the perfect mix of subject matter (big monsters who were super into professional wrestling), genre (3D fighting game), and time period (licensed games were still, like… a thing). It was the kind of game that could dominate a pizza-filled sleepover weekend or become your personality for an entire summer. One friend’s parents bought it for them, and that copy became communal: a holy thing, carried from place to place. Maybe it’s fitting that it’s back now in the form of Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered, 24 years later. The world (and Godzilla) has changed a lot, but original developer Pipeworks is still at the helm. It somehow feels just as relevant now as it did then, just in different ways, and revisiting it was a joy even removed from the nostalgia.

There is no one-to-one equivalent for what Destroy All Monsters Melee is, but the idea is pretty simple: you pick one of 12 monsters from Godzilla’s history (up through Godzilla 2000) – Godzilla, Gigan, Megalon, Ghidorah, etc. – then choose a real-world city or iconic Godzilla location to battle it out in. You’ll fight in classic rubber suit wrestling style while dodging environmental hazards, knocking down buildings, throwing rocks and skyscrapers at each other, and squashing the annoying military forces that really would prefer if you made a mess somewhere else. Last kaiju standing wins.

Despite the name, this isn't a straight remaster. You're not just looking at uprezzed models. It looks fantastic while also maintaining the “these are guys in rubber suits drop-kicking each other” vibe that defines the films it’s based on. The audio pulls its weight, too – the soundtrack has the booming authority you'd expect from a Godzilla film, buildings crumble and collapse spectacularly, beam attacks sound powerful and painful, the radio calls from military forces in the area let you know where they’ll be focusing their fire, and the announcer is having a blast. And the monsters, of course, sound like themselves. And yeah, Godzilla makes The Noise, just like you remember, even if it’s your first time here.

All of this is held together by a spit-and-duct-tape story that's just there to get you brawling: see, there's this alien race called the Vortaak. They're little green men with funky helmets, straight-from-the-‘50s fashion sense, flying saucers, and more than a little ego. They're here to take over the Earth, and what better way to do it than mind control the frankly absurd number of kaiju that are just hanging around, ready to smash a city at a moment's notice? Unfortunately for them, whichever Monster you pick breaks free of their mind control and decides the Earth is worth saving. Driving off the Vortaak means KOing the other monsters. All in a day's work, really.

That's Adventure mode, which is one of several single-player options for you to rearrange cities in. You've also got Destruction for the score chasers, where you have to wreck a city in a time limit, a souped-up Adventure mode for monsters who are at a higher level and have better stats (which you gain from experience you earn as you play certain modes), and Survival, which is exactly what it sounds like.

Listen, you can count the number of fighting games with good single-player modes on two hands (and several of those have the words “Soul Calibur” in their titles), but what's on offer here is solid if not spectacular. You only start with five monsters and a few stages unlocked, but Pipeworks has smartly reworked this remaster so you can unlock the rest in pretty much whatever order you like. You just have to meet the requirements, which you do by playing, following rumors, and unlocking research, and you can swap what you're focusing on whenever you like.

On the one hand, yeah, it's super satisfying to unlock Ghidorah because it's Ghidorah – as soon as he stops being a silhouette I can't select and starts being a gloriously golden three-headed dragon I can take into battle, some lizard part of my brain gets very happy because I can't wait to fly around and shoot lightning with that sumbitch. On the other hand, it's mad annoying to see Rodan or Ghidorah or Mecha Godzilla in Adventure mode and have the 12-year-old who lives in my head put down his slice of pizza long enough to be like “hell yeah, I wanna play that one” and then realize I can't, especially in multiplayer. Does it give you more reasons to keep playing? Absolutely, and this stuff was part and parcel of the original experience. But man, sometimes you just wanna throw down with your friends without worrying about unlocks, you know?

Multiplayer, of course, is really what Destroy All Monsters Melee is designed for, and I'm so happy that Pipeworks has added online play in addition to the returning local options. It even works really well! Most of the matches I played pre-release were smooth, though I did suffer a few disconnects. (Almost all of which happened when I was winning or doing well – I'm not saying my boy Lucas is a fraud or anything, but…)

It's here, in the multiplayer, that Destroy All Monsters Melee really shines. People will tell you, naively, that this is a button masher with no depth. These people are foolish and wrong, and if this were a Godzilla movie, they'd got a dramatic close-up shot right before a giant monster foot turned them into paste. Can you play a chaotic four-player free-for-all where everybody is mashing? Sure. You can also do wacky team battles or square off against the never-as-challenging-as-another-person CPU (though, bafflingly, you can't mix CPU opponents with friends online; let me do a comp stomp, man!). This can certainly be a casual party game if you want it to be.

But the thing about Destroy All Monsters Melee is that there is actually quite a bit more to it. Each monster has punch, kick, and fierce attacks that you can string into combos. Tilt the left stick in a direction and you get heavy attacks. Every kaiju has an energy attack governed by an energy bar that you can use as a quick projectile or charge for a beam. You can also pick up and throw buildings and rocks, or even other kaiju. You can run, jump, fly (if your character has wings), crouch, and block.

All of this opens up most of the stuff you'd see in a traditional fighting game. Someone shoot a projectile at you? Duck it. If you've knocked another monster down, they can wake up with an attack, but if you block it or stand just outside of their range, you can punish them instead. Finishing a predictable string when an opponent is blocking means you are either getting hit or thrown for your trouble.

items.summary: Switch 2 compatible.

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/11/02/switchprocontrollerzelda-1793640811585.jpg

The recently announced The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Switch 2 Pro controller looks amazing, but it's $100. Instead, why not pick up the the original The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom Switch Pro controller for just $46.60. This is a new, open box international model that is fully compatible with your US-based Switch 2 console (Switch 2 hardware is region-free/unlocked). Most importantly, the original Switch Pro controller is compatible with the Switch 2.
The Legend of Zelda Nintendo Switch Pro Controller for $46.60

Cosmetically, the Switch Pro and Switch 2 Pro controller look very similar. Both feature the same excellent build quality and heft that sets them apart from most other third party controllers. The Switch Pro works great on the new Switch 2 console, but there are some missing features that you only get with the newer Pro controller. For example, the newer controller now has two rear paddle switches, a GameChat button, and headphone jack. Also, although the Switch Pro controller supports HD rumble with haptic feedback, the new Switch 2 Pro controller has upgraded "HD Rumble 2". Finally, the Switch 2 Pro controller can wake the Switch 2 console, but the original Switch Pro controller cannot. If you can do without these features, you'll save $30 and still get a very cool officially licensed Zelda controller.

items.summary: Zach Cregger's Resident Evil movie crushed it at the box office, banking more than $400 million globally to be

content.v: Zach Cregger's Resident Evil movie crushed it at the box office, banking more than $400 million globally to become the most successful entry in the series ever . When will the film be available to watch at home, though?

According to Fandango , the home video release is set for November 3. That's apparently when people can buy the movie outright or rent it digitally, with a physical edition for Blu-ray coming at some point later. It will also presumably come to streaming at some point, and it should hit Netflix given the multi-billion-dollar Pay-1 deal the two companies have in place.
While we wait, Netflix just announced that director Paul W.S. Anderson's original Resident Evil, along with its follow-up, Resident Evil: Apocalypse, are now available to stream.

They join the other Resident Evil movies already on Netflix, including Resident Evil: Afterlife, Resident Evil: Retribution, Resident Evil: Extinction, and Resident Evil: The Final Chapter. The 2022 Resident Evil TV show is also currently streaming on Netflix.

While the new Resident Evil movie may be coming to home video on November 3, it's also staying in theaters. In fact, it was just announced that the movie is returning to IMAX and other premium large format (PLF) screens.

Cregger, who co-wrote and directed the new Resident Evil movie, recently discussed the backlash from the hardcore gamer community. He said he should have known better that fans of the games wouldn't embrace him and his ideas. After the movie came out and got great reviews and made tons of money, Cregger said he felt "gratified."

The filmmaker has said he has ideas for more Resident Evil movies, but he's not going to pursue them; instead, he's only going to make original, non-franchise movies going forward . His next movie, The Flood, is a sci-fi film starring Jennifer Lawrence.

content.v: The cloudy skies have cleared.

While cloud streaming has its benefits, nothing beats having a native version of a game. Guardians of the Galaxy launched on the first Nintendo Switch as a Cloud version, and that experience wasn’t really recommended. Now, the game is having an Encore Edition on Switch 2 with an actual port. It’s the same fun adventure, but with some performance caveats.

Guardians of the Galaxy follows Peter Quill as Star-Lord, as he travels the galaxy with his ragtag team of heroes: Rocket Raccoon, Drax, Groot, and Gamora. It starts out as a scrappy adventure of them trying to get out of debt, but eventually becomes much more engrossing and deeper as it progresses. It’s a story about friendship and teamwork that hits all the right notes.

others.title: 《如龙》系列创作者名越敏郎的工作室在发布游戏之前正式关闭

content.v: Six months after the disappearance of Nagoshi Studio's website, a Google-translated notice in the Japan government's Kanpo website (via Gematsu ) says the company has now officially closed its doors.

Founded by Yakuza creator Toshihiro Nagoshi in 2021 after a run of more than 30 years at Sega, Nagoshi Studio's first game was revealed at the 2025 Game Awards as Gang of Dragon—although the reveal was really just a brief CGI clip of Ma Dong-Seok that could have been lifted straight from Korean action film The Outlaws.

The wheels came off just a few months later, though, when NetEase pulled funding for the studio, amidst a broader pullback from external studio support over the previous year. Nagoshi Studio reportedly had no success finding another benefactor to fill the gap, and two months later, in May, the studio's website disappeared .

No official proclamations about the fate of the studio were forthcoming, though, and the Steam page remained online, so faint hope of a last-minute rescue persisted. Now, I'm afraid even that's gone, although the Steam listing is still up if you want to poke around at what might have been.
Better idea: Just watch The Outlaws.

items.title: Turtle Beach Command 系列 MC7 评测
items.summary: How much is a touchscreen really worth to you?

content.v: I must admit, I was mighty intrigued by the idea of a modern mouse (and all their high DPI machinations) with a screen slapped on the side, but I must also admit I thought we would be over the growing pains by now, what with screens being slammed into everything from cases to coolers to controllers.
Yet one look at the Turtle Beach Command Series MC7 suggests those growing pains are still being suffered. And using the mouse only confirms it.

But I get the idea in concept. I'm a big fan of my Stream Deck, and find myself regularly using its many controls. Being able to shove those into the side of the mouse with clarity to read what they're doing is intriguing. It's also particularly effective when it comes to swapping DPI, polling rate, and even checking the battery. Those are things that do benefit from a visual component. And yet a few weeks with the MC7 have convinced me I won't be making the swap full time.
Buy if…
✅ You gotta have a large screen on your mouse: As far as I can see, this is the only gaming mouse with modern specs and a big screen from a reputable brand out there.
Don't buy if…

❌ You want a mouse for competitive gaming: The MC7 is simply not comfortable nor snappy enough for competitive gaming ❌ You don't need a large screen on your mouse: We've seen small OLED screens from the likes of SteelSeries and CoolerMaster if you're simply looking for something to display figures.

Internally, the MC7 has impressive stats. Its Owl-Eye Optical sensor goes all the way up to a max DPI of 30,000, and the polling rate of 8,000 Hz is competitive-level. That's so high, in fact, that the average person won't even see the benefit of it.

And the elephant in the room here: the 2.25-inch colour display is touch-sensitive too, which means you can flick through a couple of different screens depending on your use case. We have seen screens on gaming mice before, like the Cooler Master MM830 and SteelSeries Rival 710 (neither of which are touch screens), but as far as I can tell, the MC7 is the largest on a modern gaming mouse from a reputable brand. That makes it an oddity at the least.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/w9Dy3EoWsX6eaDaEVRrCna-1920-80.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/ezp7xv5zboramJmffMpGKc-1920-80.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/PuV3MAou88jBtv7GDuPE4c-1920-80.jpg

But that's not all the MC7 has going for it. The 4D scroll wheel means you can go up, down, left and right on a page with just the wheel, and you have extra buttons here, too. You have one at the bottom of the thumb rest, another next to the mouse wheel, plus two on the left-hand side, as well as your standard clicks.

It's a wireless mouse, so it comes with a 2.4 GHz receiver, and it also has hot-swappable batteries. The battery charger has a spare USB Type-A port, which means your charger can also be the receiver. This is a sweet system, which makes the MC7 feel like it has infinite battery (as long as you are willing to spend twenty seconds swapping the battery every 10 or so hours).
Performance

The Owl-Eye sensor is great. It's consistent and smooth, and never posed any problems in any of the games I threw this mouse at. For everyday gaming, I don't have any complaints about how its internals performed. It's a slightly customised version of the PixArt PAW3950 sensor, and will be familiar to anyone who's used the Razer Deathadder V3 Pro, which previously had the exclusive use of PixArt's 30K sensor.

The mouse clicks are a tad loud for my liking, but they're plenty snappy. This bad boy is fitted with Titan Optical switches, and they are perfect under my fingertips. I have yet to hit a single double-click and find them to be very responsive.

However, the biggest problem with performance is how the MC7's weight is balanced and how it feels under the palms. At 135 g grams, it's a fairly heavy mouse (more so than the recent Naga V3 Pro and its mountain of buttons), but this wouldn't be too big of a problem if it could balance that weight in a comfortable way.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/vD6bxaDXoWTpg2Ra9AeQoA-1920-80.png
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/xtCz82ceDbkEFLdTqpTAnA-1920-80.png
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/Khx2BrpmWBjjVJBJZT2auA-1920-80.png

However, it feels clunky, and even has a slight rattle at high speeds. This all contributes to a mouse that feels a little lacking in competitive play, even though it's got the internal chops to handle everything on paper.

In use, the screen is rather peculiar. Via the Turtle Beach Swarm II software, you can flit between a few screens, which you customise with your own controls, and they are fairly snappy and responsive. However, having to arch my fingers to actually click on the screen means it's not intended for quick play. That makes it better as a micro function, or a way of displaying battery (but the device's lighting can already indicate battery life and DPI setting). It can display things like health and ammo in Counter-Strike 2, but its viewing angles are pretty poor, meaning it doesn't offer much of a tactical advantage.
Battery Life

The MC7 comes with two 1000 mAh batteries, both of which are hot-swappable. They connect to a charger (which also has a USB port for your 2.4 GHz connector), and this means you technically only need one USB to do everything for your mouse. It's a great system.

To swap the batteries out, you simply take off a compartment where your palm rests, pull the battery out and put a new one in. The MC7's onboard battery is just big enough that I've never noticed the device dying while I'm changing batteries. It's pretty sweet, and with a little practice, it can be swapped in seconds. It's not quite as quick to swap as the Glorious Model O Eternal , with its open battery system, but it is a bit tidier.

Working on my PC every day, then gaming most nights, I found myself swapping out the battery every few days at 1,000 Hz polling, which is perfectly solid given how convenient swapping the batteries is.

items.summary: Developer S-Game's action-RPG Phantom Blade Zero launched on October 29 and had a massive start across PC and

content.v: Developer S-Game's action-RPG Phantom Blade Zero launched on October 29 and had a massive start across PC and PS5.
The game sold more than 4 million copies over its first 72 hours. That works out to 926 units sold per minute or about 15.4 per second over the first three days.
"Thank you everyone from the bottom of our hearts for all the love and support," the studio said in a social media post.
The 4 million figure counts copies sold across both PC and PS5--the game is not available on Xbox. The game reached a record of 833,921 peak concurrent users on Steam on November 1.
The game's developer is based in China, and the majority of preorders for the game came from China, Taiwan, and Hong Kong.

Phantom Blade Zero's sales out of the gate are strong, but do not come close to another hit game from the Chinese game developer scene, Black Myth: Wukong. That game sold 10 million copies over its first three days . The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom, meanwhile, sold 10 million copies in three days as well.
If you’re looking to get started, you can check out our Phantom Blade Zero guides hub for many walkthroughs on increasing your power and finding rare items.
“S-Game’s Wuxia-inspired combat puts you in the middle of a Chinese action movie,” Richard Wakeling wrote in GameSpot’s Phantom Blade Zero review .

items.summary: Ink's awakening. The latest Ask the Developer interviews are positively packed with interesting tidbits about

content.v: Ink's awakening.

The latest Ask the Developer interviews are positively packed with interesting tidbits about the making of Ocarina of Time on Switch 2. One such story is all about the game's reimagined visuals, which Nintendo was even kind enough to share some initial sketches of.

According to Art Director Aya Shida, the team was consciously fighting a battle between making the game more realistic with the improved power of the Switch 2, and retaining the spirit of the original — a somewhat dark world, filled with weird characters. She therefore relied on phrases like “a puppet-show feel” and “the analogue feel of practical effects films” during development to reflect the goal: "both create a convincing sense that the characters truly exist within their respective fantasy worlds".

items.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Foil Cover Preorders Sell Out at Amazon – Here's Where You Can Still Get a Copy Before Release
items.summary: Physical copies of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake with a textured foil cover have sold out at Ama

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/09/10/zelda-59-88-2-1789037892180.png

The Switch 2 remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is set to release this Thursday, November 5. The first batch of physical copies of the game includes a textured foil cover – but these will only be available while supplies last.

That day has come at Amazon ; the retailer sold through its supply of textured-foil-cover copies over the weekend. Thankfully, if you haven’t preordered it yet and you want a copy with a reflective cover, you can still preorder it at a few retailers ( see it at Walmart ).
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (Switch 2) with Foil Cover

While the foil cover is available at several retailers, Walmart is the only one offering a $10 preorder discount. So if you want a foil cover edition of the game, and you want to save $10, you should absolutely preorder it from Walmart before it’s gone. I’d do it ASAP if I were you.
The textured foil on the cover creates a sparkling reflection effect when you rotate the game case in the light. You can see what it looks like up close in Nintendo's Instagram post below.

Amazon’s listing for the Ocarina of Time remake has a note saying it will be “available again starting Nov. 5,” but I’m fairly certain the new stock will have a standard, non-textured, non-foil cover.

Nintendo is going all out on the Ocarina of Time remake by releasing a host of Zelda-themed consoles and accessories alongside it (see our preorder guide for full details). But as these things tend to do, nearly all of the additional items sold out long ago. Some will be available again at certain retailers on November 5 – including at Best Buy’s midnight launch for the game – so not all hope is lost if you haven’t been able to lock in a preorder.
https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/11/02/textured-foil-ocarina-1793631844656.webp

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is one of the few games publishers are bold enough to release in November, ahead of the November 19 release of Grand Theft Auto 6. Most of the year’s biggest games have been bunched into September and October, or are being pushed to the early months of 2027. Check out the full upcoming release schedule for the biggest games to see what’s coming and when.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is a Switch 2-exclusive remake of the classic 1998 Nintendo 64 game of the same name. It features updated graphics and controls, plus a slew of quality-of-life improvements to make it playable and enjoyable in the modern gaming era. Check out our preview for more information.

items.summary: The start of the month is a good time to be an Xbox Game Pass subscriber, as that's when Microsoft reveals the

content.v: The start of the month is a good time to be an Xbox Game Pass subscriber, as that's when Microsoft reveals the next batch of games coming to the service. November is frontloaded with new game releases before November 19-- we can't imagine why --and several of them are day-one releases.
Kicking things off is the online horror co-op game Pit of Goblin. This has been in early access since 2024, and November 3 marks its 1.0 release.
https://www.gamespot.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Warhammer-Survivors.jpg?w=636

Next up is Escape Academy 2: Back to School on November 5. This is a day-one release, and it's all about exploring a campus, escaping life-threatening puzzle rooms, and uncovering a deadly conspiracy. November 10 will be a big day for Warhammer fans, as Warhammer Survivors launches. It's Vampire Survivors with a grimdark spin, so expect dozens of characters and weapons to master in this bullet-heaven game.

Hope in the City launches on November 11, and this stylish game follows a young girl as she searches for her parents in Shenyang's seedy underbelly. items.title: 白手起家的百万富翁表示购买 GTA 6 可以节省 5,000 美元
items.summary: British self-made millionaire, entrepreneur, and social media educator Mark Tilbury put out a video giving the

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/11/02/gta-6-1793635899315.png

British self-made millionaire, entrepreneur, and social media educator Mark Tilbury put out a video giving the most sound financial advice of 2026: buy GTA 6 . According to him, it’ll save you a big chunk of change.

“GTA 6 costs $99.99,” he said, going straight for the more expensive Ultimate Edition rather than the $80 standard edition (perhaps he, like many others, consider the Ultimate Edition and its extra contents to be the default version). “If it takes you 80 hours to complete, that’s $1.25 per hour of fun. But once you add in side missions and explore the map, it’s down to 50 cents an hour.

“Now let’s say you play for four hours every evening, that’s 50 nights of entertainment. Compare that to going out, where you could easily spend $100 in a single night. That’s why buying GTA 6 actually saves you $5,000.”

Obviously the video is tongue-in-cheek and not actual financial advice (who’s going out 50 nights in a row and spending $100 a pop?). But it’s actually a fair point on the value proposition of the game. An investment in your time, if you will.

That’s why publishers are reportedly hoping GTA 6 sets a new precedent on game pricing — other companies will struggle to compete with its size and scale. It seems like the kind of game you could play for hundreds of hours, and that’s before GTA Online even comes into the equation.
“I’m a 40yo gamer, don't drink much, don't smoke, don't do drugs or go out with friends,” said one commenter. “This is how I explain me gaming to people.”
“Straight to mum,” said another. “Rockstar paid a billion dollars for it, so it’s a steal at the end of the day,” said another mathematician.
Tilbury is a businessman best known for his videos on frugal living. Despite being a millionaire, he reuses old cups, flies economy, wears the same rotation of clothes, and avoids luxury hotels.

We’ve got plenty more on GTA 6 while you wait for its November 19 release date, including an unlikely gameplay reveal in the latest episode of South Park , how GTA 6 named one of its biggest mechanics after a beloved GTA 4 meme , and how GTA 6's map will open up relatively early and let you explore freely .

items.title: GTA 6 购买指南：为贴纸冲击做好准备
items.summary: Rockstar's GTA 6 finally releases on November 19, and if you're looking to play the game, you'll also need a c

content.v: Rockstar's GTA 6 finally releases on November 19, and if you're looking to play the game, you'll also need a console--and those are more expensive than ever. Here's a quick buying guide to help you understand what you need and how much the items will cost.
A console

First, you'll need a PlayStation 5 or Xbox Series X|S console. The least expensive option for buying a new system outright is the Xbox Series S, which costs $500. Unfortunately, that's $200 more expensive than the system cost at launch in 2020--there are a number macroeconomic and AI factors that drove prices up significantly .

A new Xbox Series X, meanwhile, costs $750 for a system with no disc drive, or $800 for a console with a disc drive. GTA 6 is not available on a disc, but having a disc drive may still be important to you for other games and media like DVDs and Blu-rays.

Switching to PlayStation, the least expensive system on Sony's side is the $600 digital edition, scaling up to $900 for a PS5 Pro (with a disc drive). PS5 Pro, as the most powerful of these options, is likely to provide the best experience from a technical and graphical standpoint, although the gameplay itself should be identical across all platforms.

These are all prices for brand-new units, but Sony offers certified refurbished PS5 consoles starting at $500. A certified refurbished Xbox Series S, meanwhile, goes for $400. These are the prices from Sony and Microsoft directly , but you can find secondhand consoles at a variety of other retailers, along with places like eBay, Facebook Marketplace, and Craigslist. As usual, check your local or preferred retailer to see the latest prices.

New and certified refurbished consoles come with everything you need--including the system, controller, and power cords. You will need a TV or monitor, but the odds are good that if you're looking to play GTA 6, you probably already have one.

People on platforms outside PlayStation and Xbox are out of luck, as GTA 6 has not been announced for Switch 2 or PC. A PC edition is expected to release in early 2027 , but there is no word on a Switch 2 version.
The game

To play GTA 6 you will need to buy GTA 6. The game's standard edition goes for $80, with its Ultimate Edition selling for $100. As mentioned, the game is not available on a disc. That being said, retailers are selling the $80 edition in stores, though you only get a code in the box. The $100 edition appears to be exclusive to digital storefronts.

The $100 Ultimate Edition includes loads of extras , including a variety of cosmetics and even in-game shops that people who buy the $80 edition cannot access. Since GTA 6 is a digital-exclusive game, there is no reason to worry about units selling out, but if you do want to preorder, you get the Vintage Vice City Pack and a free month of GTA+.
GTA 5 launched at $60 back in 2013--adjusted for inflation, that's about $85 today.

You will also need an internet connection to install GTA 6, since it's a digital only game. It's a beefy one, too, weighing in at a reported 201GB . Thankfully, preloading begins on November 12 , a full week before the game launches. That means you'll be able to begin downloading it early in the hopes of being ready to go on November 19.

November 12 is also when GTA 6's code-in-a-box copies will be available to buy at physical stores. You're not getting a week of early access, though, as the game does not unlock fully until November 19.
Do you need PS Plus or Game Pass?
GTA 6 is a strictly single-player game, and as such, you likely will not need PlayStation Plus or Xbox Game Pass to play. Rockstar has yet to confirm this, however.

Rockstar is surely going to release a new version of GTA Online at some point-- some believe that will happen in early 2027 . And at that point, you'll likely need a membership. But for launch, there is no online or multiplayer support, so we don't think a subscription to PS Plus or Game Pass would be required.
Why no disc?

Neither Rockstar nor studio owner Take-Two have provided a reason for GTA 6 being a digital exclusive, but the answer seems pretty obvious: It's all about money. Rockstar makes more money from digital game sales, and having no disc eliminates the secondhand market.
“A disc can be resold or rented a hundred times, and Rockstar earns nothing after that first sale," Rhys Elliott of Alinea Analytics said.
https://www.gamespot.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Jason_and_Lucia_02.jpg?w=636

The code-in-a-box strategy for physical games has been around for a long time already , and while people might complain online about the lack of a physical edition of GTA 6, the game is going to sell phenomenally no matter what, Mat Piscatella of Circana says.

Beyond these factors, consumer spending patterns have trended increasingly toward digital since the early 2010s. GTA 6 is such a large game in terms of its file size , so making it digital-exclusive also saves Rockstar and Take-Two money by not needing to print a second disc , if one was ever needed.
